_readme: NOMOS-SPEC-009 0.2.0 §6.5 certificate selection. For each case, the certificates available to a carrier (by where they came from) and the kids the Act relies on; `expected` is the closure an implementation must present, as sorted SPEC-007 §5.4 fingerprints, or presentable:false when it exceeds 20. Keys are from published seeds: never trust material.

cases.name: large_pool_one_approver
cases.description: An issuer pool of 32 certificates, far over 20: the sealing key, one witness, and fifteen people each with an enrolment key and a device key. The Act relies on the seal, the witness and person 7's device. Its closure is 4 certificates.

cases.name: key_certified_by_two_parents
cases.description: The approver's key is certified twice, by the root and by an intermediate. Both paths are presented, so the relying party evaluates both (SPEC-008 §4.4) and the carrier chooses neither.

cases.name: cycle_terminates
cases.description: A certifies B and B certifies A; the root certifies A. The closure from B takes all three and stops.

cases.name: chains_returned_with_statements
cases.description: The issuer pool holds only the sealing key's certificate. The witness returns its chain with its testimony and the approver returns hers with her consent (§4, §5). The closure is drawn from all three.

cases.name: unrelated_certificates_left_out
cases.description: Certificates for keys the Act does not rely on, and for other people, are not presented.

cases.name: duplicate_presented_once
cases.description: The witness returns the same certificate the issuer pool already has. It is presented once.

cases.name: closure_over_twenty_is_not_presentable
cases.description: The sealing key sits under 21 intermediates: its closure is 22 certificates. The Act cannot be presented, and the carrier must not drop certificates to fit.
